entries.name: Fraud risk assessment
entries.definition: A structured review that identifies where and how fraud could occur in an organisation and how likely and damaging it would be.

entries.name: Fraud risk management
entries.definition: Identifying, assessing and controlling the risk of fraud against an organisation.

entries.name: Free body diagrams
entries.definition: Sketches of one body isolated from its surroundings that show every force and moment acting on it, used to solve mechanics problems.

entries.name: Free Lossless Audio Codec
entries.definition: An open, royalty-free format for compressing digital audio without losing any of the original data.

entries.name: Freight handling
entries.definition: Loading, unloading, moving and securing freight at docks, warehouses and terminals.

entries.name: Freight handling equipment
entries.definition: Equipment used to move and load freight, such as forklifts, pallet jacks, conveyors and dock levelers.

entries.name: Freight inspection
entries.definition: Checking shipments for damage, correct count and conformity with shipping documents when they are received or sent.

entries.name: Freshchat
entries.definition: A messaging and live chat product from Freshworks that businesses use to talk with customers.

entries.name: Frisby.js
entries.definition: A Node.js framework for writing tests of REST API endpoints.

entries.name: Frontify
entries.definition: A cloud platform for brand management that stores brand guidelines and assets and shares them across teams.

entries.name: Fuel cell
entries.definition: A device that converts the chemical energy of a fuel, commonly hydrogen, directly into electricity through an electrochemical reaction.

entries.name: Full-cycle sales
entries.definition: Handling the whole sales process alone, from finding prospects through negotiation to closing the deal.

entries.name: Full-stack observability
entries.definition: Observability across every layer of a system, from infrastructure and network to applications and user experience.

entries.name: Full-stack software engineering
entries.definition: Building both the user-facing front end and the server-side back end of software.

entries.name: Functional Independence Measure
entries.definition: An 18-item clinical scale that rates a patient's need for help with daily activities, used mainly in rehabilitation.

entries.name: Fuse ESB
entries.definition: An open-source enterprise service bus based on Apache ServiceMix, from FuseSource and later part of Red Hat Fuse.

entries.name: Gait training
entries.definition: A physical therapy technique that helps people relearn or improve walking.

entries.name: Gallio
entries.definition: An open-source test automation platform for .NET that runs tests written with several test frameworks, including MbUnit.

entries.name: Game art
entries.definition: Creating the visual assets of video games, such as characters, environments, props and effects.

entries.name: Game design
entries.definition: Designing the rules, mechanics, systems and content of a game.

entries.name: Garment alterations
entries.definition: Adjusting finished garments, for example by hemming or taking them in or out, so they fit a customer.

entries.name: Gas meter systems
entries.definition: Devices and supporting systems that measure, record and report the gas a customer uses, including mechanical and smart gas meters.

entries.name: Gastric bypass surgery
entries.definition: A bariatric operation that makes a small stomach pouch and reroutes the small intestine to limit how much food is eaten and absorbed.

entries.name: Gatsby
entries.definition: A free, open-source framework built on React for making fast websites and apps, often from content sources such as CMSs and Markdown files.

entries.name: Gel electrophoresis of nucleic acids
entries.definition: A laboratory technique that separates DNA or RNA fragments by size by pulling them through a gel with an electric field.

entries.name: Gemology
entries.definition: The study, identification and grading of gemstones.

entries.name: General administrative and clerical tasks
entries.definition: Routine office work such as filing, data entry, answering phones and keeping records.

entries.name: General anaesthesia
entries.definition: Giving and managing drugs that put a patient into a reversible, unconscious state with no sensation, so that surgery can be done.

entries.name: General finance
entries.definition: The broad field of how money is raised, invested and managed by individuals, businesses and governments.

entries.name: General Packet Radio Service
entries.definition: A packet-switched mobile data service for 2G and 3G GSM networks, defined in standards from ETSI and 3GPP.

entries.name: General sciences
entries.definition: A broad introduction to the natural sciences, such as biology, chemistry, physics and earth science.

entries.name: Generalized linear model
entries.definition: A statistical model that extends linear regression to outcomes that are not normally distributed by using a link function.

entries.name: Generative AI
entries.definition: Methods for learning models that generate new content.

entries.name: Generic Routing Encapsulation
entries.definition: A tunnelling protocol, defined in RFC 2784, that wraps packets of one network protocol inside IP packets so they can cross another network.

entries.name: Gensim
entries.definition: A Python library for topic modelling, document similarity and word embeddings on large text collections.

entries.name: GeoDjango
entries.definition: A module included with Django (django.contrib.gis) that adds support for geographic data, spatial databases and spatial queries to web applications.

entries.name: Geographic coordinate system
entries.definition: A reference system that gives any position on the Earth's surface by latitude and longitude.

entries.name: Geologic modelling
entries.definition: Building computer models of rock layers, faults and other subsurface structures to understand the geology of a site.

entries.name: Geospatial data
entries.definition: Data that describes the location and attributes of features on the Earth, such as vector maps and raster imagery.

entries.name: Geospatial databases
entries.definition: Databases that store and index data tied to places, such as points, lines and polygons, and answer spatial queries.
